alignments.note: The fronted object marker is rendered by “for,” the preposition attaching the redemption object to the governing construction.
The construct noun takes its supplied English definite article and “redemption.”
English writes only one article for the reordered numeral, before “two hundred”; that article corresponds to s010.

Hebrew “three and seventy” and ASV “threescore and thirteen” partition seventy-three differently, so the expression is indivisible. I included “of” because this numeral expression is the nomen rectum of “redemption”; a lexical split between “seventy” and “threescore” would leave the ten incorporated into “thirteen” unaccounted for.
The reordered English numeral has no separate article before “threescore.”
This waw joins the two-hundred group to the remaining seventy-three, matching the first English “and.”
The single English article stands before the corresponding “two hundred” group.
The Hebrew dual numeral is rendered “two hundred.”
The article on the substantival participle is rendered by the relative “that.”
The participle is rendered by the copular expression “are over.”
The comparative preposition is expanded as “and above the number of”; “above” carries its relational lexeme, while “the number” makes the implicit comparison standard explicit.
The anarthrous construct substantive takes the supplied “the”; in “first born,” “first” carries the distinctive firstborn lexeme.
As the nomen rectum of “firstborn,” the construct noun takes “of”; its English definite article is supplied.
As the nomen rectum of “children,” Israel takes “of.”

review_notes: The ASV margin offers the alternative construction “those that are to be redeemed.” The alignment follows the main text’s nominal “redemption” and relative clause while preserving the same Hebrew token partition.
